about: Results of the AI editorial review for articles published with the automated label. Not a person's review.

entries.notes: All cited R&A pages downloaded and text-extracted (USGA pages 403 to scripts; R&A text is the jointly published 2023 Rules). Verified: Rule 1.1, 1.2a/b, 1.3b, 1.3c(2) three penalty levels; 3.3b/3.3c (higher score stands, lower disqualifies, 2023 unknown-penalty exception, Committee adds up); 4.1b (14 clubs, 2 strokes per hole, max 4); 5.6b (40 seconds, play through); 6.1b; 6.3c; 6.4a and 6.4b(2) ready golf; 9.4b exceptions; 12.2b; 13.1; 14.3b drop from knee height; 16.1, 16.3; 17.1d; 18.2, 18.3; 19.2/19.3; 21.2 Maximum Score; Definitions (74 defined terms, so 'more than 70' holds; teeing area two club-lengths deep; boundary stakes white); MLR E-5 purpose and 'not appropriate' for elite events (Committee Procedures 8); 'next edition published 1 January 2028' from The R&A's 14 Jan 2026 Model Local Rules article. Corrected: handicap cap now says par + 5 while establishing a Handicap Index and net double bogey afterwards (ROH Rule 3.1a/b); it had said net double bogey only, which is wrong for exactly this beginner audience. 'Paths' made 'paved and other artificially surfaced paths' (Obstruction definition) in body and takeaway. App sentence matches dump-catalog (no swing meter, shot chosen from hole/lie/distance/wind/conditions/strengths, both lines viable, fictional tours). Distinct from golf-scoring-explained, whose 'Penalties, briefly' only names the costs. Similarity max 0.023, preflight clean, publish dry-run blocked only by the absent shared log file; in-memory planBatch run passes every other check. No calculator link added.

Verified against R&A text: Rule 17.1a-e, 17.2a (R&A diagram: four options, playing 4th), 17.2b (two strokes in total), 17.3 (no ACC/embedded/unplayable relief; dangerous animal exception); Penalty Area definition (all water incl. dry ditches, edge by stakes/lines/physical features such as beach or desert, stakes are obstructions, unmarked colour = red, usually-dry ditch may be general area); Known or Virtually Certain (95%, only information found in the three-minute search); Rule 14.6; Clarification 14.3b(4)/1 (drop almost a club-length beside the line is a wrong place); Rule 1.3b(2) reasonable judgment; Rule 25.4m (four club-lengths); Club-Length definition; Committee Procedures 2C (most areas red, yellow for a carry such as a stream in front of a green, keep back-on-the-line possible or add a dropping zone, all-red allowed, red and yellow stakes side by side at a transition, green-topped stakes for no play zones, avoid red/yellow for boundaries); MLR B-2, E-1, E-5. Corrected the opening definition: it said any other area 'the Committee marks with red or yellow stakes or lines'; now 'any other part of the course the Committee defines as one, usually marked with red or yellow stakes or lines' (definition wording). Worked example counts checked (playing 3rd). App sentence matches catalog. Distinct from golf-course-management-basics (avoidance strategy, no relief procedure). Similarity max 0.026, preflight clean, dry-run clean apart from the absent shared log.

Verified against R&A text: Rule 18.1, 18.2a (three minutes, identification time, all of ball outside the edge), 18.2b, 18.3a-c (announcement wording, same distance or farther, nearer-hole consequence, indistinguishable balls, abandonment); Rule 6.4c and 6.4d(2); Rule 14.6; Definitions of Lost (partner included, declaring does not make it lost, deliberate delay, interruptions), Out of Bounds (course-side edge, stakes and line out, white), Boundary Object, Stroke and Distance; MLR A-4 incl. A-4.2 from January 2026 and the unauthorised 'crossed and came back' rule; MLR E-5 (purpose, relief-area geometry, two strokes 'comparable' to stroke and distance, not for penalty area or unplayable, provisional limits, not for elite events, WHS guidance). Count table checked. Rules-history PDF downloaded and text-extracted: confirms USGA 1946 distance-only for out of bounds, The R&A's experimental code four years later (lost, out of bounds, unplayable) and the unified code of 1 January 1952 reverting to stroke and distance. Corrected: the article said the Rules 'have kept both halves since' 1952, but the same PDF records the USGA's 1960 distance-only experiment for lost and out-of-bounds balls (provisional ball abolished), ended a year later; added that and removed the false claim. 18.2b exception reworded as optional ('you may'), not automatic. Takeaway 'the first is lost' changed to 'out of play even if you then find it' (18.1, 18.3b). App sentence matches catalog. Similarity max 0.026, preflight and dry-run clean apart from the absent shared log.

Verified against R&A text: Rule 19.1-19.3 (player alone decides, not in a penalty area, three options, ball's spot needed for back-on-the-line and lateral, spot directly below a ball in a tree, same-area limits, one-stroke bunker drops stay in the bunker, 19.3b two strokes), Rule 25.4n, Rule 16.1a(3) and 16.1f(2), Rule 14.3c (drop twice, then place), 14.6, 14.7a. Corrected: the FAQ 'Can you drop out of a bunker for one stroke?' answered 'Not under the unplayable Rule', which is wrong because one-stroke stroke-and-distance can return you outside the bunker; rewritten. A 'wrong place' bullet about dropping outside a bunker for one stroke (really a scoring error when the drop is back on the line) replaced with lateral relief outside the bunker, which is a genuine wrong place. The putting-green paragraph implied the fringe is covered because 19.2 covers the putting green; rewritten (the fringe is general area). Worked example reworked so both routes reach comparable clean lies within two club-lengths, and the principle restated precisely; 'It exists for' (an implied rule intent) changed to 'It is the escape route'. Bunker takeaway tightened. App sentence matches catalog. Distinct from golf-course-management-basics. Similarity max 0.026, preflight and dry-run clean apart from the absent shared log.

Verified against R&A text: Rule 16 purpose, 16.1a(1)-(3), 16.1b-f, 16.2 (example animals, cactus excluded, penalty-area options), 16.3 (own pitch-mark, below ground, sand exception, not-embedded cases, reasonable conclusion), 16.4 (one stroke without reasonable belief); Definitions of Obstruction (artificially surfaced roads and paths, sprinkler heads, drains, irrigation boxes), Ground Under Repair (Committee holes but not aeration holes, piled material, animal habitat), Temporary Water (merely wet or muddy ground, dew and frost excluded), Animal Hole (worms, insects, footprints), Nearest Point of Complete Relief (club, stance, swing, line; rehearsal recommended not required; relates only to that condition), Club-Length, Integral and Boundary Object; R&A diagram 16.1a (stance interference puts the point farther away); Committee Procedures 2 (GUR commonly white or blue, red and yellow avoided); MLR F-2 incl. the TV-only F-2.3 option, F-5 2+2 relief and its January 2026 GUR extension, F-6. Cart-path geometry for a right-handed player checked. Corrected: 'Model Local Rules that were last updated in January 2026' was wrong, since The R&A's 1 July 2026 Additional Clarifications revised MLR M-4; now 'several of which were added or amended from 1 January 2026'. App sentence matches catalog; the golf-career-sim-guide link is to a published guide. Similarity max 0.019, preflight and dry-run clean apart from the absent shared log.

Verified against R&A text: Rule 3.2a(1)-(4) (holes won and halved, match won when leading by more holes than remain, tied match extended hole by hole in the usual order as a continuation of the round), 3.2b (concessions clearly communicated, cannot be declined or withdrawn, agreeing to concede holes to shorten a match disqualifies), 3.2c (declared handicap too high disqualifies if it changes strokes, too low is used; lower net score wins), 3.2d(1)-(4) (strokes taken, penalties and the opponent-knew exception, 'all square', agreeing to ignore a Rule); Rule 4.1b match adjustment (max two holes); Rule 6.4a honour and cancelling a stroke; Match Play and Scorecard definitions (no card required); Committee Procedures 5A(6)a (tie, set start hole or fixed extra holes; no stroke-play play-off for a match); ROH Appendix C (singles 100%, Four-Ball match play 90%, Foursomes 50% per its worked examples; lowest plays off zero, others get the difference) and Appendix E (holes ranked relative to par, spread so strokes can be used before a match is decided, SI 1 repeats as 19). Wikipedia: Match play (dormie, strategy), Glossary (dog licence 7/6, vaulting dormie, all square, half), Playoff (golf) ('at the 19th'), 2023 Ryder Cup tables (1 up, 2 & 1, 3 & 2 and halved all present; event named only for notation). Hole-by-hole table recomputed; the 'two shapes' rule, the 10 and 8 maximum and the 18th-tee outcomes checked by enumeration. Corrected the garbled 'after the 10th, with nine or ten holes in hand' to 'on the 10th green, nine or ten up with eight to play'. Added one link to /tools/golf/course-handicap-calculator/ in the handicap section, which genuinely helps a reader turn a Handicap Index into a Playing Handicap. App sentence matches catalog and does not suggest the game has match play. Distinct from golf-tournament-formats (one paragraph on match play) and golf-scoring-explained (brief comparison). Similarity max 0.018, preflight clean, dry-run clean apart from the absent shared log.

Verified against R&A Committee Procedures 5A(6) (Terms decide ties; stroke-play tie not decided by a match and match tie not by a stroke-play play-off; what the Terms should set for a play-off; one-eighteenth of handicaps for a one-hole play-off; stroke index used for Four-Ball, Par/Bogey and Stableford; matching scorecards last round/9/6/3/18th then the first nine's 6/3/1, tie or random method, fewer than 18 holes adjusted, holes 10-18 etc. for multiple-tee starts; one-half/one-third/one-sixth deductions for net individual stroke play; count-back for other places), 5A(8) (method changed only in exceptional circumstances, weather example), 5A(3) (cut ties stated in the Terms), 5G(1) (draw-qualifying ties), Rule 3.3a and 3.2a(4). Wikipedia Playoff (golf): sudden death most common in stroke play, 2/3/4/18-hole aggregates, 18-hole play-offs held the next day, sudden death after a level aggregate, count-backs used where competitors are unavailable. Worked count-backs checked (25 v 26; 44-9=35 v 42-6=36). Toy model kept, because it answers the page's 'does sudden death favour the better player?' question with arithmetic a reader can follow; figures recomputed exactly (sudden death 60.0%, three-hole aggregate 62.4%, eighteen-hole 73.7%). Rewritten so the assumptions are explicit (independent holes, one-stroke margins, 30/20/50 per hole), the edge is translated into about 1.8 strokes per 18 holes, the three-hole calculation is shown (44.1% + 30.5% x 60%), and the table is labelled as model output, not data on real golfers or playoffs. No betting framing. App sentence matches catalog (cuts, leaderboards, ties, playoffs; rankings, earnings, next season) and says the article does not describe how the game settles ties. Distinct from how-a-golf-cut-works (who continues, not who wins). Season-long tour 'playoffs' excluded as brand-specific. Similarity max 0.015, preflight clean, dry-run clean apart from the absent shared log.

Definitions verified against Wikipedia's Glossary of golf (green in regulation 'at least two fewer than par', fairway hit on par 4s and 5s, scramble, up and down, sand save, putt 'a shot played on the green', collar slightly higher than the green) and R&A text (Rule 13.1a any part touching; Putting Green definition, edge where the prepared area visibly starts; Rule 2.2 and the 74 defined terms, none of which is 'fairway'; ROH Par definition, two putts). Arithmetic checked (14 fairway chances with four par 3s; 1/14 = 0.071). Duplication with strokes-gained-for-club-golfers (nearest existing) fixed: the closing app section restated that article's 'seven skills are attributes, not statistics' point almost word for word, so it was replaced with a distinct angle (penalty strokes as the column that records decisions, catalog-supported); the GIR 'three-footer v sixty-footer' example and 'records that something happened without recording how well' echoed that article and were reworded. Unsourced claim fixed: 'handicap built from your best recent rounds' now states the best 8 of the most recent 20 score differentials and cites ROH Rule 5 (Handicap Index Calculation), added as a source after opening it. Named the 2023 Rules edition for Rule 13.1a. The article defines the traditional stats and how to read them together; the strokes-gained piece argues for a different metric, so intents are distinct. No benchmark numbers by handicap (none invented). App sentence matches catalog. Similarity max 0.018, preflight clean, dry-run clean apart from the absent shared log.

Supersedes the earlier golf-stats-to-track entry. Edited after that hash only to add a source: The R&A's 'New and Updated Model Local Rules for 2026' (opened today), which names the 2023 Rules of Golf and says the next edition is published on 1 January 2028, so the article's '2023 Rules of Golf' wording is now cited. Everything in the earlier entry still applies: definitions checked against the Wikipedia Glossary of golf and R&A Rule 13.1a, the Putting Green definition, Rule 2.2 and the ROH Par definition; arithmetic (14 chances, 1/14) checked; the near-copy of strokes-gained-for-club-golfers' 'attributes, not statistics' section replaced with a distinct, catalog-supported decisions angle; two echoed phrasings reworded; the handicap claim made specific (best 8 of the most recent 20 score differentials) and cited to ROH Rule 5. Similarity max 0.019, preflight clean, dry-run clean apart from the absent shared log.

The length table was checked against Appendix F's table, which The R&A publishes only as an image (table_20.png, downloaded and read): every men's and women's range in yards and metres matches. Appendix F text verified (altitude below 2,000 ft/610 m; elevation, forced lay-ups and prevalent wind; 470/400-yard overlap example; design intent; the 410-yard forward-tee example; Course Rating-par adjustment only where associations include it). ROH definitions verified (Par, Authorized Association or club adjudicates par, Course Rating, Slope Rating, scratch 0.0, bogey player about 20.0 men and 24.0 women, net double bogey); Appendix G (evaluation of difficulty for scratch and bogey players; altitude among playing-length factors); Appendix E (stroke index ranks difficulty relative to par); ROH Rule 3.1b (net double bogey, lowest score earning zero Stableford points); Rule 21.1b and the Wikipedia Stableford table (2 points for par, 1 for one over, 0 worse); Wikipedia Par (score) for course par as the sum of hole pars; Scottish Golf History for Doleman's 1870 'par' of 49 for Prestwick's 12 holes and the USGA's 1911 distances. Thought experiment checked (par 5 to par 4 lowers net double bogey by one; a 5 drops from 2 points to 1). Corrected: 'as published by The R&A in October 2026' (wrong; it is merely the version checked) now 'as The R&A publishes them (checked on 2 October 2026)'; the 28-word near-verbatim definition now quotes 15 words with attribution; 'the idea behind them ... has stayed put' (unsupported) changed to par keeping its link to expert play, from 1870's 'perfect play' to today's scratch player; Doleman retelling cut to one sentence (it repeats why-golf-has-18-holes; pair similarity fell from 0.023 to 0.013); named the 2023 Rules edition for Rule 21.1 and cited The R&A's 2026 Model Local Rules article for it. Added one link to /tools/golf/course-handicap-calculator/, which includes the Course Rating-par term the paragraph describes. App sentence matches catalog. Distinct from golf-scoring-explained, which only defines par. Similarity max 0.019, preflight clean, dry-run clean apart from the absent shared log.

Verified against Scottish Golf History's '18 Hole Round' page: the early-courses table row by row; St Andrews 12 holes with 10 played twice for 22; the 1764 merger producing 18 over 10 holes; the 1842 rule quotation (repeated 1858 and 1875); Prestwick 12 holes in 1851 and 18 in 1882; the 1857 double greens with white and red flags; Muirfield 18 holes in 1891; 25 years to reach 18 courses with 18 holes; the Open rotation comparison; half of British courses 9-hole in 1919; 'stipulated round' only in 1950; 'partly at least an accident of history'. Its terms page: Rotherham's 1890 ground score, Great Yarmouth's 'Bogey man', Gosport's Colonel Bogey, The Field of 2 January 1892, mid-20th-century US use of bogey, Doleman's 1870 par, Ab Smith's 1962 recollection (1898/9) and the club's 1903 date, Darwin's 1913 quotation, eagle by 1919, albatross first referenced 1929 and the 1931 Durban press report, condor, Wethered's 'curlew'. Wikipedia Par (score): the Crump version and 1899, The Field of 28 November 1891 (Gosport), eagle 'relatively large bird', recreational golfers scoring over tightened US pars, condor 'unofficial'. The R&A/USGA rules-history PDF (downloaded and text-extracted): 13 Articles of 1744 for a single day's competition at Leith. Rule 1.1 and the Round definition; ROH Rule 3.2 on 9- and 18-hole scores. Corrected: 'by the end of the 19th century the leading clubs all played 18 holes' overstated the source; now 'by 1891 the three clubs that hosted the Open all played 18 holes'. Named the 2023 Rules edition and cited The R&A's 2026 Model Local Rules article for it. Quotations are short and attributed; disagreements between accounts are shown, not resolved. App sentence matches catalog. Distinct from golf-scoring-explained (defines the terms; this covers their documented origins). Similarity max 0.013, preflight clean, dry-run clean apart from the absent shared log.
